newsitem.title: CHINA: China says studying Vietnam proposals on oil clash.
newsitem.headline: China says studying Vietnam proposals on oil clash.

text.p: China said on Tuesday it was considering suggestions from Vietnam on how to resolve a dispute over a potentially oil-rich offshore area claimed by both sides.
Hanoi has called for immediate and unconditional meetings to resolve the territorial row sparked by the positioning of a Chinese drilling rig in the disputed waters off Vietnam's coast.

"On conflicts with other countries, China's principled stance is always to resolve them through peaceful consultations," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing in Beijing.
"We are currently studying Vietnam's other proposals," he said, but gave no details.
Vietnam turned up the heat this week, accusing its giant neighbour of violating international law and calling for urgent talks.
China responded that the area in which it was drilling was within its own territory and its actions were beyond reproach.
The oil exploration dispute is the latest in a series of territorial rows between the two communist neighbours, which fought a brief but bloody border war in 1979 and clashed at sea in the 1980s.

Amid signs of growing official frustration, a Vietnam Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday that China's positioning of the Kan Tan 111 exploration rig off its coast could not be addressed through routine border discussion channels.
"We request an expert-level meeting at the soonest moment without preconditions to discuss the issue," he said.
A senior official of Vietnam's state oil firm Petrovietnam said Hanoi would not consider a production-sharing deal with Beijing in the area.
The Chinese rig is drilling some 64.5 nautical miles off central Vietnam.

"Vietnam would never sign a contract on production-sharing with China on its continental shelf," Petrovietnam director Vu Van Mao told reporters. "If someone came to your country and drilled, and then asked you to sign a contract, would you?"
